# canvas-lms-student-mcp

> Canvas LMS MCP is a free, open source, read only MCP server that lets AI apps (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Copilot and others) read a student's Canvas LMS by Instructure courses, due dates, grades and announcements. It cannot submit, edit or delete anything. It can save your due dates as an .ics calendar file on your own computer.

Version: 0.1.5

## Setup
- Needs CANVAS_BASE_URL and CANVAS_API_TOKEN.
- Create a token in Canvas under Account, Settings, New Access Token.
- Run with npx -y canvas-lms-student-mcp. Run `npx canvas-lms-student-mcp doctor` to check the setup.

## Tools (thirteen read only, one writes a calendar file)
- get_my_courses: List your active Canvas courses with their Canvas course IDs. Use a course ID or a course name in the other tools. Example: "What are my Canvas courses this term?"
- get_todo: Your Canvas to-do list: assignments and discussions Canvas says still need attention, with due dates. Example: "What does Canvas say I still need to do?"
- get_upcoming_due_dates: Upcoming assignments and events across every Canvas course, soonest first. Example: "What is due in Canvas this week?"
- get_missing_assignments: Past-due Canvas assignments you have not submitted, with the course and the day each was due. Example: "What am I missing in Canvas?"
- get_assignments: Assignments for one Canvas course. Pass course_id as the Canvas course ID or as the course name, for example "Networking 1", and get due dates, points and submission status: not submitted, submitted, graded, missing or excused. Set bucket to filter, for example overdue. Example: "Which Canvas assignments in Networking 1 are overdue?"
- get_my_grades: Your current grade in each active Canvas course from the Canvas gradebook, with the assignments behind each grade: your score, the points possible and the submission status. Pass course_id as the Canvas course ID or as the course name to limit the grades and the breakdown to one course. Example: "What is my grade in each Canvas course and which assignments make it up?"
- get_course_content: Modules and module items for one Canvas course. Pass course_id as the Canvas course ID or as the course name. Example: "Show me the Week 3 module in my Canvas Networking course."
- get_syllabus: The syllabus text for one Canvas course, with HTML removed. Pass course_id as the Canvas course ID or as the course name. Example: "What does the Canvas syllabus say about grading in Scripting?"
- get_announcements: Recent Canvas announcements, either for the course_ids you pass or for all your active courses. Each course id can be the Canvas course ID or the course name. Example: "What did my instructors announce in Canvas lately?"
- get_whats_new: One catch up across your Canvas courses: announcements posted in the last few days, assignments graded in that window and discussions that still have unread replies. Pass since_days to change the window, 7 by default, or course_id as the Canvas course ID or as the course name to check one course. Example: "What's new in Canvas since last week?"
- get_discussions: Discussion topics for one Canvas course, with unread counts. Pass course_id as the Canvas course ID or as the course name. Example: "What discussions are open in my Canvas Networking course?"
- get_calendar_events: Canvas calendar events and assignment due dates. Pass start_date and end_date as YYYY-MM-DD to limit the range. Example: "What is on my Canvas calendar between 2026-10-01 and 2026-10-31?"
- get_target_grade: Work out what score is needed on the remaining Canvas work in one course to reach a target percent. Pass course_id as the Canvas course ID or as the course name and target_percent as a number from 0 to 100. If Canvas reports a current percent for that course, pass current_percent to use it instead of computing from graded points alone. Example: "What do I need on the rest of my work in Networking 1 to get an 85 percent?"
- export_due_dates_calendar: Build an iCalendar (.ics) file of Canvas due dates and calendar events that opens in Google Calendar, Apple Calendar and Outlook. Give a folder in path and the file is saved there, or leave path out and the calendar text comes back so you can save it yourself. Each event carries the course name, the points, the submission status and a link back to Canvas, plus a reminder the day before. By default only work you still owe is in the file, set include_submitted to add the work you already handed in. Use days_ahead to change how far ahead to look, 30 days by default, or course_id as the Canvas course ID or as the course name for one course. Example: "Put my Canvas due dates in Google Calendar."

get_assignments takes an optional bucket filter, for example overdue. get_announcements takes optional course_ids. get_whats_new takes an optional since_days. get_calendar_events takes optional start_date and end_date as YYYY-MM-DD. export_due_dates_calendar takes optional days_ahead, course_id, include_submitted, path and filename.

A course can be named instead of numbered. Give the Canvas course ID or the course name, for example "Networking 1", wherever a tool takes course_id or course_ids. The name is looked up in the list get_my_courses shows, and a name that fits no course says so and points at get_my_courses.
